entries.title: Psalms 48:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The city - In Jerusalem. Mountain - In his holy mountain.

entries.title: Psalms 48:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The joy - This is spoken prophetically, because the joyful doctrine of the gospel was to go from thence to all nations. The city - Of God, who justly calls himself a great king.

entries.title: Psalms 48:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Known - By long experience. Palaces - Possibly he may point at the king's palace and the temple, which was the palace of the king of heaven; which two palaces God did in a singular manner protect, and by protecting them, protected the whole city and people.

entries.title: Psalms 48:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The kings - Either those kings confederate against Jehoshaphat, 2Chron 20:1 , or the Assyrian princes; whom they vain - gloriously called kings, Isa 10:8 . Passed - In their march towards Jerusalem.

entries.title: Psalms 48:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Saw it - They did only look upon it, but not come into it, nor shoot an arrow there - nor cast a bank against it, 2Kings 19:32 . Marvelled - At the wonderful works wrought by God.

entries.title: Psalms 48:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Fear - At the tidings of Tirhakah's coming against them, 2Kings 19:9 , and at that terrible slaughter of their army, ver. 35.

entries.title: Psalms 48:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Breakest - Thou didst no less violently and suddenly destroy these raging enemies of Jerusalem, than sometimes thou destroyest the ships at sea with a fierce and vehement wind, such as the eastern winds were in those parts.

entries.title: Psalms 48:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Heard - The predictions of the prophets have been verified by the events. Establish - God will defend her in all succeeding ages. And so God would have done, if Jerusalem had not forsaken him, and forfeited his protection.

entries.title: Psalms 48:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Thought - It hath been the matter of our serious and deep meditation, when we have been worshipping in thy temple.

entries.title: Psalms 48:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: So - Thou art acknowledged to be such an one as thou hast affirmed thyself to be in thy Word, God Almighty, or All - sufficient, the Lord of hosts, and a strong tower to all that trust in thee. Righteousness - Of righteous actions; by which thou discoverest thy holiness.

entries.title: Psalms 48:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Tell - He bids them mark well her towers, bulwarks, and palaces, with thankfulness to God, when they should find upon enquiry, that not one of them were demolished.

entries.title: Psalms 48:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Tell it - That they may continue their praises to God for this mercy, by which they hold and enjoy all their blessings.
